body.x: Samsung Electronics’ latest smartphone, the Galaxy S3, will be available for viewing at KES 2012. The Galaxy S3 follows on the heels of the Galaxy S and the Galaxy S2, of which more than 50 million units were sold. By the middle of this past July, 10 million units of this new bestseller had already flown off shelves, making it the fastest mobile phone among all those released by Samsung Electronics to surpass ten million sales.

The Galaxy S3 offers a variety of features including Smart Stay, Direct Call, Smart Alert, Double Tap to Top, and S Voice. Its objective is to become a “human phone” that scores a triple play with human-centered user interface, technology, and design.

Smart Stay is a function that automatically prevents the screen from turning off when the user is looking at it by recognizing the users face and eyes. This means that when a user is surfing the net or reading an e-book on the Galaxy S3, it is no longer necessary to periodically touch the device to maintain the screen lighting. When you look away from the screen, though, it will automatically turn off. With Direct Call, if you put the phone to your ear after looking at the screen for received/sent texts or the call log screen, the phone will automatically place a call for you. Smart Alert, on the other hand, vibrates to alert you to a missed call or message. Tap the top of the Galaxy S3 screen twice to activate Double Tap to Top, which shows you a list of your most recent emails or text messages. Altogether, there are ten different motion recognition functions included on the phone. Also worthy of note is the phone’s voice recognition feature, referred to as S Voice, which allows users to control features including calls, alarms, and music playback.

With a 4.8 inch HD super AMOLED display, the Galaxy S3 is 22% larger than its predecessor, the Galaxy S2. In addition, it features Pop Up Play, a function that allows you to view a movie at the same time as you are composing a text message or surfing the web. The 8.0 megapixel camera on the back of the phone incorporates Burst Shot, which takes twenty frames in a row, and Best Photo, which automatically selects the sharpest picture for you. It has also become much more convenient to share files with your friends. S Beam allows Galaxy S3 users to use NFC (near-field communication) and WiFi Direct to share a high-definition movie (1GB) in three minutes or a MP3 music file (10MB) in two seconds, while AllShare Play is an easy and convenient way to share media between your various smart devices, just two more of the phone’s diverse functions. The Galaxy S3 comes in two colors, pebble blue and marble white.
